title: Right exact functors extend across Brown infinity localization
statement:
Use quasicategories, nerves, mapping spaces and coherent functor categories of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], in a universe containing the categories involved. Let $\mathcal A$ be an ordinary category with an initial object $0$ and classes $C,W$ containing isomorphisms and closed under composition. Assume $W$ is retract closed and has two-out-of-three, every $0\to X$ lies in $C$, every arrow factors as a member of $C$ followed by a member of $W$, pushouts of members of $C$ along arbitrary arrows exist and belong to $C$, and pushouts of members of $C\cap W$ belong to $C\cap W$. Let $q:N\mathcal A\to L$ be a localization: for every quasicategory $\mathcal D$, restriction identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal D)$ with the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(N\mathcal A,\mathcal D)$ inverting $W$.
Assume $L$ admits finite coherent colimits. Let $\mathcal E$ be a quasicategory admitting finite coherent colimits, meaning colimits of diagrams indexed by simplicial sets with finitely many nondegenerate simplices. Let $T:N\mathcal A\to\mathcal E$ send $W$ to equivalences, send $0$ to an initial object, and send each ordinary pushout square along a member of $C$ to a coherent pushout square. Then the factorization $\overline T:L\to\mathcal E$ furnished by the entire-functor-category localization property preserves finite coherent colimits.

source.place: Dual of Proposition 7.5.6 (last assertion), printed pp. 372-373; right exactness is dual to Definition 7.5.2. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result. Read online on 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: First establish the precise pushout cocones supplied by localization. Pass to $\mathcal A^{op}$, with terminal object $0$, fibrations $C^{op}$ and weak equivalences $W^{op}$. The factorization reverses to a weak equivalence followed by a fibration; every terminal map is a fibration; and the two pullback-stability assumptions are exactly the opposites of the two pushout-stability assumptions. Thus [lem-coef-brown-fibrant-localization-pullbacks] applies. Taking opposites gives a localization $q':N\mathcal A\to L'$ sending $0$ to an initial object and each pushout along $C$ to a coherent pushout. Here opposite simplicial sets are formed by reversing the ordinals: this exchanges inner horns and identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(U^{op},V)$ with $\operatorname{Fun}(U,V^{op})^{op}$. It therefore exchanges the defining cone and cocone categories and preserves the localization universal property. To check the mapping-space convention in this reversal, [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] identifies right-pinched spaces with arrow mapping spaces; ordinal reversal identifies the latter with the reversed arrow spaces, whose realizations are homeomorphic by reversing barycentric coordinates. Hence the contractibility defining initial and terminal objects is exchanged as required. Since $q$ and $q'$ have the entire-functor-category localization property, factor each through the other. Full faithfulness of restriction lifts the identity comparisons to coherent natural equivalences of the composites with the identities. This gives an equivalence $L'\simeq L$ compatible with $q',q$. An equivalence and its quasi-inverse induce inverse equivalences on cocone categories; by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] they preserve initial objects there. Consequently $q0$ is initial in $L$, and the actual image under $q$ of every ordinary cofibration pushout square is a pushout cocone.

source.place: Proposition 7.5.6, first part, dualized; Definition 7.1.2 for uniqueness of localization. Agent expansion of opposite and cocone conventions.

proof.text: Let $K$ be the span shape and $d:K\to L$ any coherent span. By [lem-coef-brown-left-fractions] choose $A,X,Y$ and equivalences from its vertices to $qA,qX,qY$. Lift these vertex equivalences by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], giving an equivalent span $d_0=(qX\xleftarrow{\alpha_0}qA\xrightarrow{\beta_0}qY)$. The same fraction node gives $[\alpha_0]=[q(s)]^{-1}[q(f)]$ and $[\beta_0]=[q(t)]^{-1}[q(g)]$, where $f:A\to Z_x$, $g:A\to Z_y$ and $s:X\to Z_x,t:Y\to Z_y$ lie in $C\cap W$. Thus $(1,[q(s)],[q(t)])$ is an isomorphism in $hL$ from $d_0$ to the strict span $qN(D)$ with $D=(Z_x\xleftarrow f A\xrightarrow g Z_y)$. Apply [lem-coef-brown-span-coherent-rectification] to lift it to a coherent equivalence, hence $d\simeq qN(D)$. Factor $f$ as $A\xrightarrow i X'\xrightarrow p Z_x$ with $i\in C,p\in W$. The strict span $D'=(X'\xleftarrow i A\xrightarrow g Z_y)$ maps to $D$ by $(p,1,1)$; its image under $q$ is an equivalence by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. The pushout $P=X'\amalg_A Z_y$ exists since $i\in C$, and step 1 makes its specified cocone on $qN(D')$ colimiting. Thus every coherent span has such an equivalent pushout model.

source.place: Proposition 7.5.6, proof on printed p. 373, dualized: fraction representation of spans followed by cofibration factorization.

proof.text: Write $F=\overline T$ and let $\beta:Fq\simeq T$ be the localization comparison. Given a specified pushout cocone $\sigma:d\to\Delta_Kp$, step 2 supplies a canonical pushout cocone $\lambda:c\to\Delta_K(qP)$ and an equivalence $e:d\to c$. Apply [lem-coef-brown-cocone-equivalence-transport] to $e$ and $1_p$: it supplies a full cocone equivalence $H:\sigma\simeq\sigma_0$, where $\sigma_0:c\to\Delta_Kp$ is colimiting. Then $\sigma_0$ and $\lambda$ are initial in the same cocone category. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] they are connected by an equivalence of cocones, whose apex component is an equivalence. The natural equivalence $\beta$, restricted to the whole ordinary pushout cocone, compares $F\lambda$ with its $T$-image, with diagram and apex components equivalences. That $T$-image is colimiting by the hypothesis along $i\in C$. Apply the invariance clause of the transport node to obtain colimitingness of $F\lambda$, then $F\sigma_0$ using the equivalence of cocones, and finally $F\sigma$ using the image of $H$. This preserves the full specified cocone. Also $F(q0)\simeq T0$ is initial. Cone calculus makes any initial object of $L$ equivalent to $q0$, and the initial-object mapping-space criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-terminal-pullback-criterion], dualized, transports initiality of their images. Thus $F$ preserves every initial object.

source.place: Proposition 7.5.6, last assertion, printed p. 373 (dualized); explicit cocone and natural-equivalence argument.

proof.text:
The pushout $B\amalg_0 D$ in either $L$ or $\mathcal E$ is a binary coproduct. Indeed the dual mapping-space criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-terminal-pullback-criterion] gives, for every target $z$,
$$\operatorname{Map}(B\amalg_0D,z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(B,z)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}(0,z)}\operatorname{Map}(D,z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(B,z)\times\operatorname{Map}(D,z),$$
since $0$ is initial and its mapping space to $z$ is contractible. The equivalence is induced by the two cocone legs, hence is the coproduct universal property by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Step 3 sends the defining square to a pushout square over the initial object $F0$, so it sends these same two legs to coproduct legs. Starting with the empty coproduct $0$ and adjoining one summand at a time proves preservation of coproducts indexed by every finite set: at the induction step the mapping space out of the iterated binary coproduct is the product of the mapping spaces out of all summands, with its specified projection maps. Uniqueness of initial objects in each cocone category then gives preservation for every coproduct cocone, independently of the chosen ordering or binary presentation.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.28, finite-product reduction used in its proof, dualized; binary coproduct argument from the mapping-space criterion (Theorem 6.6.9).

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-limits-products-pullbacks] with $\kappa=\aleph_0$ to $F^{op}:L^{op}\to\mathcal E^{op}$. Its existence hypotheses hold because $L$ and $\mathcal E$ admit colimits of all simplicial diagrams with finitely many nondegenerate simplices, and ordinal reversal preserves this finiteness. Step 3 gives preservation of pullbacks after reversal, and step 4 gives preservation of products indexed by every finite set, including the empty product. The cited node explicitly includes $\kappa=\aleph_0$ and concludes preservation of all such limiting cones. Reversing again, using the cone/cocone and mapping-space identifications of step 1, shows that $F$ sends every finite coherent colimiting cocone to a colimiting cocone. This is exactly preservation of finite coherent colimits by $\overline T$.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.28 applied to opposites, as used in Example 7.5.4 and the last assertion of Proposition 7.5.6.
